newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to talk to France about Dassault papers.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to talk to France about Dassault papers.

text.p: Belgium's justice minister says he plans a new approach to the French government in quest of information Belgium seeks on allegations that French defence firm Dassault bribed Belgian political parties to secure a defence contract.

"We have not received all the documents we requested," Stefaan De Clerck told Belgian newspaper Le Soir in an interview published on Friday, adding he planned to send a letter to his French counterpart Jacques Toubon about the matter.
"We are trying to put together a file as it should be done -- exchanging information, taking positions, reacting and getting things moving," he said.
This is not the first time De Clerck has intervened to speed things up. In February Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said he was ready to put pressure on France.
In January a French court gave Belgian police some of the papers they requested more than a year earlier, after the Belgian justice minister personally contacted Toubon.

Police are investigating claims Dassault paid 600 million Belgian francs ($17 million) in kickbacks to Belgian political parties to secure a 1989 contract to fit air defence systems to the country's F-16 fighter jets.

After months of lying dormant the "Dassault affair" sprang to life again at the start of the year and even threatenend the stability of Belgium's centre left government when top francophone socialist party officials were arrested on corruption charges in connection with the investigation.
A Belgian court last year issued an international arrest warrant for Dassault, the group's founder and chairman, who has denied all wrongdoing but has refused to come to Belgium to answer questions.
De Clerck told Le Soir he knew Dassault was "an important man in France". Asked if he thought the chairman was close to the French authorities he replied: "That's what is said."
